sm: The hosts open the Friday, November 13th episode by previewing the day's stories. NVIDIA shares have cratered after its CEO resigned amid more allegations, raising questions about the chip and AI landscape and possible political fallout. President Trump has pulled Vice President Vance from the Iran talks, saying the country does not need a deal, while gas prices keep dropping. A migrant caravan in southern Mexico is also heading toward the United States, testing the president's resolve on the border.

Culture reporter Megan Basham explains that Jensen Huang, who co-founded NVIDIA 33 years ago, is out as CEO. Days earlier the plan was for him to stay while the board investigated whether his relationship with an alleged Chinese spy created national security risks. Then the New York Times reported he also had an affair with a health care vice president who reported to him, and there are reports of a possible third affair. Chief financial officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO. A tech industry voice says the change may be advisable but the board must choose a successor carefully.

The discussion turns to political fallout. Reports say Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confronted Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over why Megaspeed, an NVIDIA customer linked to Chinese espionage, was not placed on a federal restriction list despite earlier briefings. Attorney General Todd Blanche said the Justice Department will look at possible export law violations, which could be civil or criminal. President Trump is standing by Huang, calling him honorable. NVIDIA fell 14 percent at Thursday's open before partly rebounding, CoreWeave fell too, competitors gained, and many retirement accounts are exposed.

Cabot Phillips of Wired In says Trump's removal of JD Vance from Iran negotiations followed last Tuesday's midterm results. The Wall Street Journal had reported Vance was lead negotiator, preparing more face-to-face meetings with Iranian officials. Trump posted that Vance will instead focus on corruption and crime in Democrat-run cities and states, and that we do not need a deal with Iran. Trump has said Vance was right that the Iran war drove the blue wave, though he maintains the war was worth it.

Phillips also covers a report that Treasury Secretary Bessent moved onto a military base after credible threats against his life. Rubio, Hegseth and new chief of staff Stephen Miller also live on bases. The UN General Assembly voted 144 of 193 to reconfirm Iran's seat on a committee reviewing women's rights and terrorism policy, and only the US, Canada and Australia have publicly objected. Finally, gas prices are falling because of seasonal shifts and cheaper crude tied to optimism over diplomacy. Analysts warn prices would rise if hostilities resume, and falling below pre-war levels would require the conflict to end.

Tim Pierce reports on a caravan of 1,500 to 2,000 people, mostly on foot, that left Tapachula in southern Mexico on Tuesday. The border is about a thousand miles away, with up to 700 more miles depending on the crossing point, so it is months from arriving. Migrants told CNN they hope Democratic gains in Congress will soften enforcement. Border czar Tom Homan says elections do not change laws, the border will stay secure for two years, and migrants will not be released.

Trump posted that the migrants will not be accepted, that Mexico must stop them, and that tariffs on Mexico will double if it does not. Homan said Mexico should put troops on its southern border and noted it is illegal to transit Mexico without a visa. Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum replied that no caravan has reached the US border since January 2025 and that Mexico is relocating migrants or keeping them. Breitbart reports one caravan received a police escort and was allowed to stay overnight in public buildings.
